AUTUMN STORY 1

Noah

Too Old for Trick-or-Treating?
📖 Read

Halloween can be a bit of a problem when you've got two little brothers.

Don't get me wrong. I love my brothers. They're six, they're twins, and they're usually great fun. But when they get excited about something, they never stop talking about it.

This year, they wanted to go trick-or-treating. Of course, Mum thought it would be a good idea if I went with them.

I'm thirteen now, so I wasn't sure about it. Most of my mates don't go trick-or-treating with little children. They meet up with friends or go to Halloween parties.

But the twins were so excited that I agreed.

They wanted different costumes, which surprised me because they usually want exactly the same things. One dressed as a pirate and the other as a skeleton. Mum helped them get ready, and I put on a simple skeleton costume. That was enough for me.

We left the house just after it got dark.

At first, I thought the evening would be boring. The twins walked slowly because they wanted to look at every pumpkin and every scary decoration. They even stopped to count the plastic bats in someone's window.

Then we reached a house with a huge bowl of sweets.

The woman at the door gave the twins some chocolate. Then she offered me some too.

Well, I wasn't going to say no, was I?

After that, I started enjoying myself a lot more. We visited houses with pumpkins in the windows and collected all kinds of sweets. The twins sometimes forgot to say thank you because they were so excited. I had to remind them.

By the time we got home, our bags were quite heavy. Mum helped the twins check their sweets, and I made sure they didn't eat everything before bed.

I actually had a pretty good collection myself.

I wouldn't tell my mates how much I enjoyed trick-or-treating, though. Well, maybe I would if I had some chocolate left to share!

I know Halloween has a long history, but I don't know all the details. We haven't learnt much about it at school.

Bonfire Night is different.

We studied the Gunpowder Plot in history. I remember that Guy Fawkes and some other men wanted to blow up Parliament in 1605. They were caught before they could do it.

The weekend after Halloween, Dad took me to an organised fireworks display. I was staying with him, so it was nice to do something together.

We arrived early and found a good place to stand. Dad bought us something warm to eat, and we talked about school and swimming while we waited.

When the fireworks started, everyone looked up.

Some were red and gold. Others made huge circles of light in the sky. It was brilliant.

I really enjoyed being there with Dad.

So, which celebration do I prefer?

I love the excitement of Bonfire Night, but I have to admit something.

Halloween has one very important advantage.

You get to take the sweets home!

AUTUMN STORY 2

Abby

Costumes, Sweets and Sparkling Skies
📖 Read

There are lots of things I like about autumn. The colours of the trees, warm jumpers, hot chocolate and, of course, Halloween!

I love Halloween because you can be creative. You can decorate your house, make things and wear clothes you wouldn't normally wear.

My three best friends are Sophie, Lily and Grace. Every year, we try to do something special together.

This year, we decided to make our own Halloween costumes.

That sounded like a great idea until we actually started.

Sophie wanted something really impressive. Lily kept finding funny costumes online, and Grace thought we should choose something simple. I had about ten different ideas and couldn't decide which one I liked best.

Eventually, we chose our costumes and started making them.

My bedroom became a complete mess. There were clothes on the floor, paper bats on my desk and bits of black fabric everywhere. Mum wasn't surprised. She already thinks my room is too untidy.

I decided to dress as a witch, but not a really frightening one. I made a black hat and added little silver stars. It took ages, but I loved how it looked when I'd finished.

I sometimes worry about what other people think of my clothes. For a moment, I wondered if my costume looked silly. But then I remembered that Halloween is about having fun. I didn't need to look perfect.

On 31 October, Sophie, Lily, Grace and I went trick-or-treating.

We walked through our neighbourhood, admired the decorations and took a few photos. Some houses looked amazing. One family had turned their front garden into a little graveyard.

Lily made us laugh so much that we could hardly walk.

We collected plenty of sweets, but I think we enjoyed looking at the costumes and decorations even more.

I also know a little about the history of Halloween.

I read about it because I enjoy English and Art. I discovered that some Halloween traditions are connected with an old Celtic festival called Samhain. People celebrated the end of the harvest and the beginning of winter.

The name Halloween also comes from All Hallows' Eve, the evening before All Saints' Day. I think it's interesting that an old celebration has changed so much.

A few days later, it was time for Bonfire Night.

I know the basic story of Guy Fawkes because we learnt about him at school. He was involved in a plan to blow up Parliament in 1605, but it didn't work.

My parents took me to a fireworks display, and I met my friends there.

Dad tried to make funny jokes while we waited. Some were actually quite good, although I wasn't going to tell him that.

Then the sky filled with colours.

The fireworks looked like beautiful paintings that only lasted a few seconds. I wished I could stop time and look at them for longer.

Halloween and Bonfire Night are very different.

One lets me create something myself. The other lets me enjoy something wonderful with the people I love.

And I think autumn would be rather boring without them.

AUTUMN STORY 3

Ameena

Halloween in a Busy House
📖 Read

Halloween in our house is never a quiet event.

Actually, nothing in our house is ever quiet. I've got a big family, and when everyone gets excited about something, it can become a little crazy.

This year was no different.

Some of my younger brothers and sisters started planning their Halloween costumes at the beginning of October. They had so many ideas that I couldn't remember them all.

One wanted to be an astronaut. Another wanted to be a dinosaur. Someone else changed their mind about five times.

Of course, they all wanted me to help.

We don't usually buy expensive costumes. There are too many of us, and Mum and Dad have more important things to spend money on.

But I actually enjoy making things ourselves.

We found some old clothes, cardboard and paint. My older sister helped too. By the time we'd finished, we'd made some pretty good costumes without spending much money.

I decided to dress as an autumn fairy. I used an old green top, pieces of fabric and some leaves to make my costume. I even made my own wings! It looked pretty good, even if I say so myself!

On Halloween evening, I took some of the younger children trick-or-treating.

Getting everyone ready was the hardest part. Someone couldn't find their shoes. Someone else had lost their bag for collecting sweets. I felt as if I was getting everyone ready for school again!

Eventually, we left the house.

It was cold outside, but everyone was too excited to care. We visited houses with pumpkins and Halloween decorations. The younger children loved collecting sweets, and I enjoyed watching them have fun.

At one house, a person dressed as a skeleton opened the door. One of my younger brothers jumped backwards and almost dropped his bag!

I laughed so much that my stomach hurt.

When we got home, everyone wanted to show Mum and Dad what they'd collected. Our living room was full of costumes, sweets and very excited children.

I was tired, but I still had homework to finish.

Sometimes being an older sister is hard work!

I know Halloween is an old celebration, but I haven't spent much time learning about its history. I know it has changed over the years and that people didn't always celebrate it in the same way.

Bonfire Night is something I understand better.

We learnt about the Gunpowder Plot at school. In 1605, some men planned to blow up Parliament and kill King James I. Guy Fawkes was caught with gunpowder before their plan could work.

I remembered those facts quite easily. I usually do well at school, even when I don't particularly enjoy the homework!

For Bonfire Night, our family went to a local fireworks display. We brought our own snacks and stood together in the cold.

The fireworks were beautiful. The younger children loved the bright colours, and I liked having everyone together without worrying about school for a while.

Well, almost everyone. Someone still managed to lose a glove.

But that's my family.

Life is always busy, and sometimes a little messy. I wouldn't change it, though.

AUTUMN STORY 4

Luca

Two Nights, Two Kinds of Fun
📖 Read

I really like autumn. Not because of the weather, because it's usually cold and wet, but because there are two brilliant celebrations: Halloween and Bonfire Night.

Halloween is always fun at our house. My little brother Oliver starts talking about it weeks before 31 October. He's ten, but sometimes he gets more excited than a five-year-old!

This year, Mum helped us decorate the front door. Oliver wanted spiders everywhere. I thought a few would be enough, but he didn't agree. By the time we'd finished, there were spiders on the door, the windows and even Mum's favourite plant. She wasn't very happy about that last one.

On Halloween evening, Oliver and I went trick-or-treating together. He wore a skeleton costume and I dressed as a vampire. I didn't want anything too complicated. I just wanted to have fun.

Oliver knew exactly which houses had the best decorations. We walked around our neighbourhood with our bags and collected sweets. Some people had made their gardens really scary. There was even a skeleton sitting on a bench outside one house. Oliver was afraid to go near it until he discovered it wasn't real.

I enjoyed going with him more than I expected. He was so happy about every little chocolate bar that I couldn't stop smiling.

When we got home, Oliver started counting his sweets. I didn't stay for long because I was meeting Jack and Harry. We went out together, walked around town and got something warm to drink. Harry made us laugh all evening. We didn't need to spend hours on our phones. Being together was enough.

I know Halloween is an old celebration, but I don't know much about its history. I think it has something to do with ghosts and people from a long time ago. I'm sure Jack could explain it. He always seems to know things like that.

A few days later, it was Bonfire Night.

We learnt about Guy Fawkes at school. In 1605, a group of men planned to blow up Parliament, but their plan failed. That's why people remember 5 November.

Our family went to a big fireworks display. Dad and Oliver wanted to stand near the front, but Mum thought we'd get a better view from further back. She was right, as usual.

The fireworks were amazing. Oliver couldn't stop looking at the sky, and I loved the colours and the loud bangs. Afterwards, we went home to warm up.

I think that's what I like most about these celebrations. Halloween means having fun with my mates and Oliver. Bonfire Night means spending time with my family.

Two different nights, but both are brilliant.

AUTUMN STORY 5

Raheem

The Stories Behind the Celebrations
📖 Read

I think autumn is a really interesting time of year.

The weather gets colder, the leaves change colour and suddenly there are pumpkins everywhere.

But something else happens, too. People start celebrating Halloween and Bonfire Night.

I enjoy these celebrations, but there's something I like almost as much as the celebrations themselves.

Finding out why we have them.

My sister thinks I ask too many questions. She might be right.

This year, I wanted to find out why people wear frightening costumes at Halloween. I also wondered why pumpkins are such an important part of the celebration.

I started reading about Halloween and discovered that its history is much older than I expected.

One of the old traditions connected with Halloween is a Celtic festival called Samhain. It marked the end of the harvest and the beginning of winter.

Long ago, some people believed that the world of the living and the world of the dead were closer at this time of year.

I thought that was fascinating.

But Halloween doesn't come from just one tradition.

The name comes from All Hallows' Eve, the evening before All Saints' Day on 1 November. Over many years, different traditions became part of the Halloween we know today.

When I told my sister some of these facts, she wasn't nearly as interested as I was.

She was much more interested in decorating our front door.

We didn't go trick-or-treating this year. Instead, we stayed at home and gave sweets to the children who visited our house.

I helped put some pumpkins outside. My sister wanted them to look frightening, but I thought one of them looked rather friendly.

I enjoyed seeing all the costumes. Some children looked like witches, ghosts or monsters. Others had made costumes that were really funny.

By the end of the evening, we'd given away nearly all our sweets.

Then it was time to think about Bonfire Night.

This is one of my favourite historical stories.

In 1605, a group of men planned to blow up the Houses of Parliament. They wanted to kill King James I. The group was led by Robert Catesby, although Guy Fawkes is the person most people remember.

A warning letter helped the authorities discover the plot. Guy Fawkes was found guarding the gunpowder beneath the House of Lords.

The plan failed, and that's why 5 November became an important date.

What I find interesting is that people still remember something that happened more than four hundred years ago.

My dad and I looked at a map of London to find the Houses of Parliament. I'd love to visit the building one day and learn more about its history.

On Bonfire Night, my family went to a public fireworks display.

There were lots of people, colourful lights and a huge bonfire. My sister was happy because I couldn't talk about history while the fireworks were making so much noise!

The sky looked amazing.

As we walked home, I thought about how different the two celebrations were.

Halloween has changed through many centuries. Bonfire Night remembers a particular event in British history.

But both have something in common.

They connect people today with stories from a long time ago.

And I think that's pretty amazing.

AUTUMN STORY 6

Mia

Pumpkins, Plans and a Few Surprises
📖 Read

I like Halloween, but I don't really enjoy big, noisy parties.

I'd much rather spend an evening with a few good friends. I can be myself when I'm with people I know well.

This year, we decided to have a little Halloween evening at my house.

We were going to decorate pumpkins, make some snacks and watch a scary film.

It sounded simple enough.

Of course, things don't always go exactly as planned when I'm involved!

A few days before Halloween, Mum helped me write a checklist. I needed pumpkins, decorations, drinks and something to eat.

I was very proud of my list.

Unfortunately, I forgot to look at it when we went shopping.

We got home with the pumpkins and decorations, but without the popcorn.

Mum wasn't surprised.

Luckily, Dad went back to the shop, so everything was ready when my friends arrived.

We started by decorating the pumpkins.

I wanted to make a really frightening face on mine, but it didn't look frightening at all. One eye was much bigger than the other, and its mouth looked as if it was laughing.

My friends thought it was brilliant.

After that, we put our pumpkins near the window and turned on some little lights. The room looked really cosy.

Then we watched a scary film.

I sometimes find it difficult to sit still and concentrate for a long time. But when I'm really interested in something, I can forget about everything else.

That evening, I didn't even notice how quickly the time passed.

I know Halloween has something to do with old traditions, but I can't remember exactly where it comes from. There are ghosts and witches and pumpkins, of course, but I'm sure there's more to the story.

History isn't always easy for me. I sometimes remember little pieces of information and forget how they fit together.

Bonfire Night is a good example.

I remembered learning about Guy Fawkes at school, but I couldn't remember whether he actually blew up Parliament.

Dad helped me find the answer.

In 1605, Guy Fawkes and some other men planned to blow up Parliament, but they were stopped. That's why people still remember 5 November.

For Bonfire Night, Mum and Dad took me to a local fireworks display.

I enjoyed walking around before it started. There were warm drinks, people talking and children running about in their winter coats.

When the fireworks began, I couldn't stop watching.

Some made big circles of light. Others looked like bright stars falling from the sky.

I tried to remember which colours I liked best, but there were too many!

On the way home, I realised something.

I didn't need to remember every historical fact to enjoy the celebrations.

Halloween was special because I spent time with my friends. Bonfire Night was special because I spent time with my family.

Sometimes the best memories are the little things that happen when you're having fun.

And those are the things I hope I never forget.
